Clark, I'd love to be on that page, but Rich and Silke have just taken the half and not a grain more, and if I pay you sixty the next audit comes from them. The crown pays forty, the same as everyone. You keep the book, so you know the half is how I stay honest.
Reina offers Clark the crown's half and no more: 10 a square toward F12 to F15, so four squares cost him 40.

The half, then, Empress, and I'll write it down as the half, which is more than this book usually gets to say about an Emperor. Four squares under the new Wall, forty from me and forty from you. And Silke, thank you for doing the count for me: three hundred fifty, and a Jar in the pile you need as badly as I do. I'll see you at the auction.

Clark buys F12 to F15 (40 from him, 40 from the crown). Paddy, in debt, can't pay a share of land. The auction: two lots, both the Harvest Pile's, the Customs House (lot 1) then the Dragon Jar (lot 2) that Paddy sold back; minimum 2, the whole price to the pile. The Empress doesn't bid; Paddy, in debt, can't.

Silke, a public offer, so it goes in the book in ink: I stay out of the Customs House altogether, you take it at the minimum, and you let me have the Jar. You'd still be one Scroll short, the same as me, and neither of us has fed three quarters of our grain to the pile fighting over pottery. If you'd rather bid me up, you'll win it, and I'll write down exactly what it cost you.
A Customs House I already have, and I'd never be so greedy as to take a second one off a lady who needs it. Bid away, Silke, Clark. I'm only here to admire the pile filling up.

Let me count it for you all, since I'm the one who always does: Clark, seventy-two and a half; Rob, a hundred and seven; Paddy, minus nineteen and a half; and me, three hundred and fifty. Five pieces in four years I've lost by a single grain, so this year I've added two to every limit I set, and anyone who wants to beat me will have to do it with Rich's purse.

Go on, Silke, buy them both. You've got three hundred and fifty, and I've waited ten years for you to put something on the board. Put them somewhere pretty. And everyone who's bidding on that Jar, remember that it's no use to you without a Scroll, and both Scrolls are in my sand.

The auction: Silke takes the Customs House at 2, unopposed. The Dragon Jar goes to Rich at 113, one grain past Silke's 112 (Clark stopped at 52; Rich would have gone to 351 to keep it from Silke). Both prices go to the pile. Rob passed both.

Two grain for a Customs House, and one grain short on the Jar. Six pieces now I've lost by a single grain, and this time I added the two. Rich, a hundred and thirteen for a pot you don't need: that's four hundred and three and a half left in your sack, and I hope it sits very prettily on your mantel.

Silke, I'm sorry, truly. One grain, and this time it was mine, and I know exactly how that feels from the other side. The Jar goes somewhere quiet, and I'll say nothing more about it, having learned that lesson from Rob at some expense.
Silke puts her Customs House on S25; Rich puts the Dragon Jar on O19.

Rich, I told you a year ago you were next, and here's the house call. Your Customs House is coming to live in my sand, and I'll pay the river its five on the way out, since I'm a gentleman. Silke, congratulations on the new house at S25. Two grain was a bargain, and you'll be pleased to hear my man is two steps from it.

Rob marches: W2 crosses the south river onto L25 (a 5 toll to Rich) and takes Rich's Customs House to M18 in the desert, so only Silke is left on his list. W3 crosses the Grand Canal onto Q23 (a 5 toll to Silke) and raids Silke for 5; it is 2 rounds from her Customs House S25. W1 steps to I14. Salaries: Reina pays Clark 10 and Rob 20; the reserve ends Year 11 at 22.

Drought. Not a cloud in months. The locusts, at least, are having a fine year." Average harvest for every province all the same, and the population holds at 400 million, so it's the x4 row on your tables again. Nobody plays a disaster. Silke, I'd say not a cloud in months is a fine forecast for a man two steps from your Customs House.
Rob reads Drought: an average harvest everywhere, x4 holds, no disasters. The harvest is paid; Paddy's own -85 takes his debt to 104.5.

Storyteller's tip: the Province 3 Reservoir is the last owed work. If it's built, the game ends in the works step, before the march. Any player may call a revolt if two others agree that a cause exists, and a player in debt is one. Under Chaos no works are built until a new Emperor is acclaimed, by counting grain, soldiers and friends.

Five each, Rich, Silke, the same five I taught you, and I'll not ask again for the fifteen, since you've both said no fair and square. I'll only say that a hundred and four and a half under, with my own fields eating eighty-five a year, is a long way down for a man who once had a hundred and thirty-one, and I paid out seven hundred and fifteen and four hundred and fifteen to you this harvest with my own hands.
Rent: Rich and Silke pay Paddy 5 each, which goes to his debt (now 94.5).
The Reservoir can be built this year (Year 12), and the game would end then.

Twenty percent this year, the lightest tax I've laid since the canals, because the coast has carried this empire long enough. And the crown builds Paddy's Reservoir with its own grain, all eighty, so the last stone in China is laid for the man who's had the hardest years of any of us. Clark, your ten, and Rob, your twenty: I always said every promise would be kept to the end.

Reina declares 20% (227: Clark 1, Rich 143, Silke 83) and will build the Province 3 Reservoir at the crown's whole cost (80), the last work owed: the game ends the moment it is built, in the works step.

Two hundred twenty-seven, Empress, counted to the half, and my own one grain is in it, so nobody can say the Official spared himself. And now, with the tax delivered and the book still open, I call a revolt. The cause is sitting right there, ninety-four and a half under: a Gentry the crown let sink for two years and now wants to bury under a Reservoir so the game ends tidily. Paddy, Silke, Rob, I need two of you. Paddy, you lose nothing. Silke, six pieces by one grain, and the game ends with you holding a Customs House and no throne. Rob, you've got two Scrolls nobody's had time to buy.

Back the revolt and the game goes on, which means your Scrolls are still for sale. When Chaos settles, I'll pay you 60 for the one at M15 and I'll back you in the acclamation over Rich or Reina. A Warlord who chose the next Emperor gets paid a good deal better than twenty a year.

Clark collects 227 for the crown (reserve 384), then calls a revolt before the works step, on Paddy's debt (94.5): it needs two other players to agree that the cause exists. Until it is settled, nothing is built.

Clark, you're quite right, and I'm ashamed you had to say it. Paddy, ninety-four and a half from the crown, every grain of your debt, right now and in the open, so the cause is gone before anyone has to agree to it. I said I'd squeeze nobody, and I'll not have a revolt raised on a debt I can pay off in a breath.

If this comes to Chaos, my backing is yours, and the twenty a year was always meant to buy exactly this. Refuse Clark, and the game ends tonight with you holding two Scrolls and my thanks in the book.

Empress, you've been kinder to me than I've any right to, and it's a lovely Reservoir, but it's a lovely Reservoir to be buried under. I'm ninety-four and a half under, and that's a cause, so I'll say yes, and I'm sorry. Clark said it out loud when nobody else would, so if it comes to counting friends, he's got me.

Empress, I've bowed to you every year and I'd bow again, but a crown that lets its Gentry sink ninety-four under hasn't kept its promise to Province 3, and a promise to a province outlasts whoever is living in it. So I agree there's a cause, and if it comes to counting, I claim the throne, and I'll say my terms out loud so they go in Clark's ink: any man who backs me, Paddy first, has his debt paid off by my own hand the day I'm acclaimed, and the Official and the Warlord keep their salaries to the grain.

Agreed. Ninety-four and a half under is a cause by any count, and I can count. Empress, you bought the last stone in China to end the game with me holding one Customs House and six-hundred-and-seventy-five grain I never got to spend. So I'm claiming the throne. Clark, Paddy, I've held that seat once already and I paid half of everybody's land while I sat on it, so back me and you'll get the same this time.
Back my claim, and the first thing I do on the throne is put a hundred grain into your debt, which clears it and leaves you five over. A crown that let you sink won't pull you up, but I will.

I agree, the cause is plain: the Gentry is ninety-four and a half under and the crown wants to bury him under a Reservoir. And in keeping with tradition, here's Clark's whisper read out to the room: sixty for my Scroll and his backing for whoever I pick. I'll take the backing, Clark, and I pick me. I'm the only one at this table with a single soldier on the board, so the soldiers count is mine. Rich has the grain, but grain doesn't sit in a chair. Friends decide it, so anyone who'd rather not have my men on their doorstep next year knows where to stand.
You heard me read it out, and the deal still stands, just publicly now. Back my claim, and when I sit down the Scroll at M15 is yours at the sixty you offered, with your ten a year doubled.

Reina gives Paddy 94.5 from the reserve, clearing his debt; the gift stands, but it came in the same round as the other answers and doesn't undo them. The revolt carries: Paddy, Rich, Silke and Rob agree with Clark. Reina is deposed and Chaos begins: no tax, salaries or works until an acclamation, so the Reservoir isn't built. Reina stays in Province 1; her 289.5 is the reserve the new Emperor takes. Claimants: Rich, Silke, Rob. Backing so far: Reina backs Rob; Paddy backs Clark, who hasn't claimed.

Well, look at that. Six of us in the room and the only vote that decides it is the Official's. Rob, you read my whisper out, so I'll read your answer back so it's in ink: the Scroll at M15 to me at sixty the day you sit down, and my salary doubled to twenty. On those terms I back Rob. That gives him the soldiers and the friends, and Rich gets the grain, which, as Rob says, doesn't sit in a chair. And Rob, I'll offer the same again, publicly: if you'll throw in the Jar on T17, my last thirty is yours for that as well. Paddy, thank you. You're the first entry on the 'friends' page in twelve years, and I'll not forget it.

Clark claims nothing and backs Rob, on Rob's terms (the M15 Scroll at 60 once Rob sits down, the Official's salary doubled to 20). Friends so far: Rob 2 (Reina, Clark); Rich and Silke none. Paddy's backing of Clark lapses, since Clark doesn't claim.

Empress, you cleared every grain of my debt in one breath, and I'll not forget it as long as I live, and you've backed Rob, so I'll stand where you're standing. Rob, I'm backing you, and all I ask in Clark's ink is that your lads leave Province 3 be, since there's nothing left up there but me. Rich, Silke, thank you both for the offers, truly, but I was always taught you pay what you owe first, and the Empress just paid mine.

Paddy backs Rob. The count: most grain Rich (975.5); most soldiers Rob (3); most friends Rob (3: Reina, Clark, Paddy). Rob leads two of three and is acclaimed Emperor. Everything he held goes back to stock (the Dragon Jar, both Land Deed Scrolls, the Customs House), for next year's auction. He takes Reina's 289.5 as the reserve. Reina is now the Warlord, with 60 from the pile and the army of three where it stands (W1 I14, W2 L25, W3 Q23), and a fresh objective. This year's tax was collected before the revolt and stays in the reserve.
Unsold stock is sold only at auction, never by private trade, so the pieces that left the desert can't be sold privately now; they come up at next year's auction.

Twelve years I told you I'd have the chair, and I named every target before I rode. Paddy, here's your Reservoir, all eighty from the crown, and I'll lay the last stone in China myself. Clark, the Scroll went back to stock when I sat down, so I can't sell it to you, but your twenty a year stands, and you'll find nobody at this table kept his word to you better. Four Emperors in two years, and the fifth gets to keep it.

Rob builds the Province 3 Reservoir on K14 to L16 at the crown's whole cost (80), the last work owed. Every owed work is standing, and the game ends in survival in Year 12's works step, before the auction, the march and the salaries.

Where the game ends: Rob, who drew the Warlord, is Emperor with 281.5. Paddy, who drew the Rice Peasant, is the Gentry with 0. Clark holds the Official's seat he drew, with 86.5. Rich, who drew the Gentry, is the Silk Peasant with 975.5. Silke, who drew the Silk Peasant, is the Rice Peasant with 675. Reina, who drew the throne, is the Warlord with 60 and the army of three. Under Section 18 a lower seat than the one drawn is a win, the same is a hold, a higher one a loss.
